title: Standard Operating Procedure for Conducting Larval and Pupal Surveys for Anopheles
author: Tanya L L Russell

steps.title: Approach the Habitat
steps.instruction: Approach the identified potential habitat carefully to avoid disturbing the environment.

substeps.instruction: Proceed slowly and step lightly to avoid vibrating the water or disturbing vegetation.
Approach the water facing the sun to prevent casting a shadow on the water.
If wind is strong, position yourself on the windward side where larvae and pupae are most concentrated.
Visually inspect for larvae and pupae before beginning to dip.

steps.title: Collect Larvae and Pupae
steps.instruction: Sample the water using a dipper to collect larvae and pupae.

substeps.instruction: Skim the dipper head in a straight line towards the larvae, angled at 45 degrees and submerged approximately 3 cm in the water.
Perform 10 dips from each sampling station.
Wait at least 2 minutes between each dip to allow larvae to resurface.
If the water is muddy, transfer the dipper contents to a flat white tray for better visibility.
In very small habitats, use a Turkey baster (gravy needle) to transfer water to the dipper or white tray.
For large habitats, sample in multiple locations to estimate density across the entire habitat.

steps.title: Count and Record Samples
steps.instruction: Quantify the collected specimens and document the findings.

substeps.instruction: Count the number of larvae in each dip.
Record the data, including zero counts (no larvae or pupae).
Empty the water away from the aquatic habitat to avoid further disturbance.

steps.title: Transfer Samples to Vials
steps.instruction: Move collected samples into vials using a pipette.

substeps.instruction: Ensure larvae are not overcrowded in the vial.
Provide at least 2 ml of liquid per larva (e.g., a 50 ml vial containing 40 ml of water and 20 larvae).

steps.title: Transport Samples
steps.instruction: Transport the larvae while maintaining viability.

substeps.instruction: Store larvae in water from the habitat.
Keep samples cool during transport, utilizing a cooler box if necessary.

steps.title: Preserve or Kill Specimens
steps.instruction: Terminate larvae and preserve them for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Kill larvae using hot water from a kettle or by placing them in a vial with >70% ethanol.
Store samples in 70% ethanol for extended periods.
Ensure ethanol concentration does not drop below 70% to prevent decomposition.

steps.title: Document Habitat Location
steps.instruction: Record the location of the larval habitat for future surveys.

substeps.instruction: Take GPS coordinates of the habitat or create a mud map.
